amp_en.label: RF amp (14 dB)
amp_en.description: Front-end RF amplifier — adds 14 dB across the entire 1 MHz–6 GHz range. Default OFF. Flip ON for weak HF / VHF signals (FT8 / WSPR / faint VHF DX); leave OFF in strong RF environments to avoid front-end overload and intermod. Independent of the `gain` knob — both can stack.

bias_tx.label: Bias-T (TX-side DC)
bias_tx.description: Applies +3.3 V DC on the antenna port for active LNAs / preamps. Default OFF. Turn ON only when the connected antenna explicitly needs it — and verify the antenna can tolerate DC bias before flipping.

notes: 8 MS/s is comfortable on USB 2.0 and gives a useful wideband view; HackRF runs cleanly up to 20 MS/s on USB 3.0 if you want to push it. AMP off by default — flip it for weak HF/VHF signals only. Advanced panel exposes 1–20 MS/s in 1 MS/s steps via the device probe. Baseband-filter ladder (1.75–24 MHz, discrete steps from libhackrf) is used to auto-pick the closest ≤ Fs entry when the user changes the sample rate — the HackRF driver does NOT autoselect; without an explicit `setBandwidth` the filter stays at whatever was last set and aliases everything outside it.
ai_operator_notes:
**HackRF One** — half-duplex 8-bit SDR, 1 MHz – 6 GHz, sample rates 2 / 4 / 8 / 10 / 16 / 20 MS/s. Single SMA antenna port (TX/RX shared — receive-only in Ferrite, no transmit path). No AGC; gain is always manual.

### Gain — three stages, one knob

`--gain N` (and the UI slider) is the **unified front-end gain in dB**, range **0–62 dB**. The driver distributes it across LNA (0–40 dB in 8 dB steps) and VGA (0–62 dB in 2 dB steps); the actual landing value is the closest valid pair.

**Hard ceiling: 62 dB.** Values above that get rejected by libhackrf with `setGain(N) returned invalid parameter(s)` and the gain stays at the previous value. **Never request more than 62 dB.**

The RF amplifier is a *separate* setting (`amp_en`) that adds **14 dB on top** of the `--gain` knob when enabled. Independent — both can stack. Flip `amp_en=true` for weak HF / VHF / UHF DX; flip `amp_en=false` in strong RF environments to avoid front-end overload.

Gain decision tree (all `--gain` values are 0–62 dB):
- Weak HF / VHF DX (FT8, WSPR, faint signals) → `--gain 40–50` + `amp_en=true`.
- General-purpose VHF / UHF → `--gain 30–40`, `amp_en=false`.
- Strong urban RF (near broadcast towers, ISM-band repeaters) → `--gain 20–30`, `amp_en=false`. Watch the waterfall for ADC clipping (ceiling pinned at byte=255) and back off.
- ADC clipping → drop `--gain` 10 dB; if still clipped, that's `amp_en=false` territory.

```
ferrite-ctl --note "weak ISM hunt" param src amp_en=true
ferrite-ctl --note "weak ISM hunt" tune 433.92M --gain 45
```

When the explorer-prompt gain-calibration loop says "escalate after `--gain` alone has plateaued," flipping `amp_en=true` is the escalation on this driver. Don't escalate by requesting more dB on the `--gain` knob — the driver will refuse and your manual gain will stay at the pre-attempt value.

### Antenna

Single SMA TX/RX port — Ferrite drives it receive-only. Whatever the operator has connected is what you get. No port-switching to debug; if the `Operator-supplied radio setup` section below doesn't say what antenna is hooked up, ask the operator rather than guessing band fit.

### Sample-rate / IF-filter pairing

The baseband IF filter does **not** auto-track sample rate on HackRF — without an explicit `setBandwidth` the filter stays at whatever was last set. The driver-preset auto-picks the largest ladder entry ≤ Fs on rate changes, but ad-hoc `param src sample_rate_hz=...` won't refresh the filter. Pair rate changes with bandwidth changes:

```
ferrite-ctl --note "wide ISM survey" tune 433.92M --rate 8000000 --bw 5000000
```

Common working pairs: 2 MS/s / 1.75 MHz, 8 MS/s / 5 MHz (the run.sh defaults), 20 MS/s / 15 MHz.

### DC spike — zero-IF leakage

HackRF is zero-IF across its entire range. The LO leaks straight through to the ADC, producing a bright vertical line at the *tuned centre*. Park the centre on your target and the spike obliterates it.

**`dc_offset_correction` does NOT help here.** SoapyHackRF doesn't implement Soapy's DC-offset-mode interface, so the `dc` toggle won't appear in the UI for this radio and `param src dc_offset_correction=...` is a silent no-op. The only fix on HackRF is the off-tune dodge: tune the source 50–100 kHz off-target and use the channelizer's `freq_shift_hz` to pull the actual target back to baseband for demod. (Same dodge as SDRplay would need if its tracker were off.)

### Driver warnings — what to expect under `tail decoder --category driver`

- `setGain(N) returned invalid parameter(s)` — you asked for more than 62 dB. The driver refuses; the previous gain stays in effect. Re-issue with `N ≤ 62`.
- `hackrf_set_freq() failed` — frequency outside 1 MHz – 6 GHz. Re-tune.

If you see `setGain` errors hitting repeatedly with the same `N`, the gain you intended never landed — your captures are at whatever the *previous* successful gain was, not the value the AI's mental model says is current. Flag with `[REVIEW]` and back off.
